docs.title: Be Gone Unbelief My Saviour Is Near
docs.text:
Song: Be Gone Unbelief, My Saviour Is Near

Copyright Information: John Newton (Lyrics), Franz Joseph Haydn (Tune)

Lyrics: Begone unbelief, my Saviour is near And for my relief, will surely appear By prayer let me wrestle and He will perform With Christ in the vessel, I smile at the storm

If dark be my way, since He is my Guide 'Tis mine to obey, 'Tis His to provide Though cisterns be broken And creatures all fail The word He hath spoken shall surely prevail

His love in time past forbids me to think He'll leave me at last in trouble to sink While each Ebenezer I have in review Confirms His good pleasure To help me quite through.

Why should I complain of want or distress Temptation or pain? He told me no less The heirs of salvation, I know from His word Through much tribulation must follow their Lord

Since all that I meet shall work for my good The bitter is sweet, the medicine food Though painful at present, 'Twill cease before long And then, O how pleasant the conqueror's song.

Source: https://youtu.be/gUp7fkCFIs0

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 Begone unbelief, my Saviour is near And for my relief, will surely appear By prayer let me wrestle and He will perform With Christ in the vessel, I smile at the storm

Meaning: This opening stanza is a bold command to doubt and fear to leave immediately because the Saviour is near and will definitely come to help. The singer chooses to pray earnestly like Jacob wrestling with God, trusting that the Lord will act powerfully, and even in the middle of life’s fiercest storms, having Christ with him brings calm joy and confidence instead of panic.

Stanza 2 If dark be my way, since He is my Guide 'Tis mine to obey, 'Tis His to provide Though cisterns be broken And creatures all fail The word He hath spoken shall surely prevail

Meaning: Even when the path ahead is completely dark and uncertain, the singer remembers Jesus is his Guide, so his only responsibility is to obey while God handles provision. Human sources of help may dry up and people may fail, yet God’s spoken promises in Scripture will always stand and ultimately win.

Stanza 3 His love in time past forbids me to think He'll leave me at last in trouble to sink While each Ebenezer I have in review Confirms His good pleasure To help me quite through.

Meaning: Looking back at God’s faithful love in the past completely removes any thought that He might abandon the singer now. Every “Ebenezer” (stone of remembrance) from previous deliverances proves that God delights in helping His people and will carry them all the way to the end without fail.

Stanza 4 Why should I complain of want or distress Temptation or pain? He told me no less The heirs of salvation, I know from His word Through much tribulation must follow their Lord

Meaning: The singer questions why he should grumble about lack, hardship, temptation, or pain when Jesus already warned that this is the normal path for every believer. True followers of Christ must walk through many difficulties just as their Lord did, and this is clearly stated in God’s Word.

Stanza 5 Since all that I meet shall work for my good The bitter is sweet, the medicine food Though painful at present, 'Twill cease before long And then, O how pleasant the conqueror's song.

Meaning: Everything the singer encounters — even the bitter and painful things — God promises to use for ultimate good. The suffering feels like harsh medicine now, but it will soon end, and the believer will then sing a joyful victory song like a conqueror who has overcome through Christ.

Summary of Song This powerful hymn by John Newton is a strong declaration of faith and encouragement for anyone facing doubt, darkness, or difficulty. It commands unbelief to leave, recalls God’s past faithfulness, accepts suffering as part of the Christian journey, and rests confidently in the truth that every trial works for good and will end in victory. With its steady, reassuring melody, the song strengthens the heart to trust and obey, reminding believers that Christ is present in every storm and will see them through to the end with a conqueror’s song.

docs.title: God Is Here and That to Bless Us
docs.text:
Song: God Is Here and That to Bless Us

Copyright Information: John Robson Sweney, Public Domain. This recording was made at Christian Fellowship Church, Bangalore, India.

Lyrics: God is here, and that to bless us With the Spirit’s quickening power; See, the cloud already bending, Waits to drop the grateful shower.

Let it come, O Lord, we pray Thee, Let the shower of blessings fall; We are waiting, we are waiting, Oh, revive the hearts of all.

God is here! we feel His presence In this consecrated place; But we need the soul refreshing Of His free, unbounded grace.

God is here! oh, then, believing, Bring to Him our one desire, That His love may now be kindled, Till it’s flame each heart inspire.

Saviour, grant the prayer we offer, While in simple faith we bow, From the windows of Thy mercy Pour us out a blessing now.

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwyNS8qmWpg

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 God is here, and that to bless us With the Spirit’s quickening power; See, the cloud already bending, Waits to drop the grateful shower.

Meaning: This opening stanza boldly declares that God is already present in the meeting and has come specifically to bless His people. It pictures the Holy Spirit’s reviving power as a rain cloud ready to pour down refreshing showers of blessing, building an atmosphere of joyful expectation and faith.

Chorus Let it come, O Lord, we pray Thee, Let the shower of blessings fall; We are waiting, we are waiting, Oh, revive the hearts of all.

Meaning: The chorus is a collective, urgent prayer asking the Lord to send the promised blessing immediately. The repeated “We are waiting” shows eager anticipation and dependence on God, pleading for a fresh revival that will awaken and renew every heart in the congregation.

Stanza 2 God is here! we feel His presence In this consecrated place; But we need the soul refreshing Of His free, unbounded grace.

Meaning: Here the singers acknowledge that they can already sense God’s presence in the dedicated place of worship, yet they humbly confess their deep need for a greater inner refreshing. They long for the unlimited, free-flowing grace of the Holy Spirit to satisfy and revive their souls.

Stanza 3 God is here! oh, then, believing, Bring to Him our one desire, That His love may now be kindled, Till it’s flame each heart inspire.

Meaning: With faith and confidence that God is present, the stanza calls the people to bring their single, united request before Him: that His love would be stirred up like a fire and set every heart ablaze with passion for the Lord.

Stanza 4 Saviour, grant the prayer we offer, While in simple faith we bow, From the windows of Thy mercy Pour us out a blessing now.

Meaning: This closing stanza is a direct, humble plea to Jesus, the Saviour. While bowing in simple childlike faith, the people ask Him to open the “windows of heaven” and pour out His mercy and blessing right at that moment.

Summary of Song This classic revival hymn joyfully announces God’s presence in the midst of His people and earnestly pleads for the Holy Spirit to come like refreshing rain, reviving hearts, kindling love, and pouring out abundant blessings. With its simple yet powerful structure and expectant tone, the song creates a perfect atmosphere for corporate worship, inviting the congregation to wait on God together for a fresh outpouring of His grace and power. It is especially meaningful during prayer meetings, worship services, or seasons when the church longs for spiritual renewal and awakening.

docs.title: He Walked Where I Walked
docs.text:
Song: He Walked Where I Walked | God With Us

Copyright Information: Graham Kendrick. This recording was made at Christian Fellowship Church, Bangalore, India.

Lyrics: He walked where I walked He stood where I stand He felt what I feel He understands He knows my frailty Shared my humanity Tempted in every way Yet without sin

God with us So close to us God with us Emmanuel Emmanuel

One of a hated race Stung by the prejudice Suffering injustice Yet He forgives Wept for my wasted years Paid for my wickedness He died in my place That I might live

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rziwfk7_hbU

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 He walked where I walked He stood where I stand He felt what I feel He understands He knows my frailty Shared my humanity Tempted in every way Yet without sin

Meaning: This beautiful opening powerfully declares the truth of the Incarnation. Jesus did not remain distant — He entered fully into our human experience. He walked the same roads, stood in the same struggles, felt the same emotions, and faced the same temptations we face. Yet, unlike us, He remained completely without sin. He knows our weakness from the inside and still understands us perfectly with compassion.

Chorus God with us So close to us God with us Emmanuel Emmanuel

Meaning: The chorus celebrates the heart of the Christmas message and the gospel itself — “God with us.” Jesus is not a far-off God but Emmanuel, God who came near. He is so close that He shares our humanity completely. This truth brings comfort, intimacy, and awe: the holy God chose to dwell among us and remain with us.

Stanza 2 One of a hated race Stung by the prejudice Suffering injustice Yet He forgives Wept for my wasted years Paid for my wickedness He died in my place That I might live

Meaning: This stanza highlights the depth of Christ’s love and identification with the marginalized and broken. Jesus was born into a despised people, experienced racism and injustice, yet responded with forgiveness. He wept over our wasted, sinful lives and willingly took our punishment upon Himself. His death was substitutionary — He died in our place so that we might have life. This is the gospel in its most personal and moving form.

Summary of Song This powerful Graham Kendrick song beautifully captures the wonder of the Incarnation and the depth of Christ’s empathy and love. It reminds us that Jesus didn’t stay in heaven — He walked in our shoes, felt our pain, faced our temptations, experienced injustice, and still chose to die in our place. The repeated cry of “God with us… Emmanuel” anchors the song in the glorious truth that God came near. It is a deeply comforting and worshipful song that draws us to marvel at a Saviour who fully understands us and gave everything to bring us life. Perfect for Christmas, communion, or any time we need to remember how close and compassionate our God truly is.

docs.title: I Am Not My Own
docs.text:
Song: I Am Not My Own Artists: Keith & Kristyn Getty and Skye Peterson

YouTube Source: Watch on YouTube

docs.title: Lyrics
docs.text:
Stanza 1 The One who made the heavens made my heart and soul Before I drew a breath, I was loved and known I am His creation, the Maker's masterpiece And all that He designs will be done in me

Stanza 2 My body is a temple of the Living God I'll worship in this house that His blood has bought As I bear His image, oh may I not profane The holiness I hold in this earthly frame

Chorus I belong to the Lord, oh I am not my own I belong to the Lord, I am not my own I will honor Him for this I know I belong to the Lord, I am not my own

Stanza 3 And if He has redeemed me, I am not my own The measure of my worth is His love alone He declares my standing, and He declares my state So I will know myself by the name He gave

Stanza 4 I am not my own and now my heart is free O Maker come and make what You will of me There is nothing broken that You cannot repair So Lord, I leave my life in Your loving care

Final Chorus I will honor Him for this I know I belong to the Lord, I am not my own

docs.title: Stanza 1
docs.text:
The One who made the heavens made my heart and soul Before I drew a breath, I was loved and known I am His creation, the Maker's masterpiece And all that He designs will be done in me

Meaning: This verse establishes our identity as God’s deliberate creation. The same God who created the universe personally formed us and loved us even before we existed. We are not accidents but His masterpiece, and He will complete His good purposes in our lives.

docs.title: Stanza 2
docs.text:
My body is a temple of the Living God I'll worship in this house that His blood has bought As I bear His image, oh may I not profane The holiness I hold in this earthly frame

Meaning: Drawing from 1 Corinthians 6:19-20, this stanza reminds us that our bodies belong to God and are sacred temples purchased by Christ’s blood. We are called to honour Him by living holy lives that reflect His image without defiling what He has made holy.

docs.title: Chorus
docs.text:
I belong to the Lord, oh I am not my own I belong to the Lord, I am not my own I will honor Him for this I know I belong to the Lord, I am not my own

Meaning: The powerful, repeated chorus is a joyful declaration of belonging. Because we were bought with a price, we are not our own. This truth frees us to live for God’s honour and glory rather than for ourselves.

docs.title: Stanza 3
docs.text:
And if He has redeemed me, I am not my own The measure of my worth is His love alone He declares my standing, and He declares my state So I will know myself by the name He gave

Meaning: Redemption by Christ confirms our complete belonging to Him. Our value is not based on performance, appearance, or achievements but solely on His unchanging love. We find our true identity in the names and standing God declares over us.

docs.title: Stanza 4
docs.text:
I am not my own and now my heart is free O Maker come and make what You will of me There is nothing broken that You cannot repair So Lord, I leave my life in Your loving care

Meaning: Surrendering ownership to God brings true freedom. The singer invites the Lord (the Maker) to shape their life as He desires, trusting that He can heal and restore anything broken, and willingly placing their entire life into His caring hands.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
This beautiful modern hymn is a powerful declaration of belonging to God and finding true identity and freedom in Him. It reminds us that we are lovingly created, redeemed by Christ’s blood, and called to live as holy temples that honour the Lord.

With its clear biblical truth and tender melody, the song encourages complete surrender — “I am not my own” — leading to a life shaped by God’s loving design, healing, and purpose.

It is especially meaningful for personal devotion, teaching on identity in Christ, or worship services focused on surrender and holiness.

Copyright Information: Keith & Kristyn Getty and Skye Peterson.

docs.title: Let Your Living Water Flow
docs.text:
Song: Let Your Living Water Flow

Copyright Information: John Watson. This recording was made at Christian Fellowship Church, Bangalore, India.

Lyrics: Let Your Living Water Flow Over My Soul, Let Your Holy Spirit Come And Take Control, Of Every Situation That Has Troubled My Mind, All My Cares And Burdens On To You I Roll.

Jesus, Jesus, Jesus. Father, Father, Father

Come Now Holy Spirit And Take Control, Hold Me In Your Loving Arms And Make Me Whole, Wipe Away All Doubt And Fear And Take My Pride, Draw Me To Your Love And Keep Me By Your Side.

Spirit, Spirit, Spirit Father, Father, Father.

Give Your Life To Jesus, Let Him Fill Your Soul, Let Him Take You In His Arms And Make You Whole, As You Give Your Life To Him, He’ll Set You Free, You Will Live And Reign With Him Eternally.

Jesus, Jesus, Jesus. Spirit, Spirit, Spirit

Let Your Living Water Flow Over My Soul, Let Your Holy Spirit Come And Take Control, Of Every Situation That Has Troubled My Mind, All My Cares And Burdens On To You I Roll.

Source: https://youtu.be/1T5dEaBvDkA

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 Let Your Living Water Flow Over My Soul, Let Your Holy Spirit Come And Take Control, Of Every Situation That Has Troubled My Mind, All My Cares And Burdens On To You I Roll.

Meaning: This opening stanza is a heartfelt prayer inviting the Holy Spirit’s refreshing presence into the singer’s life. “Living Water” refers to the life-giving, cleansing power of the Holy Spirit that Jesus promised. The singer asks the Spirit to take full control over every troubling situation and worry, then deliberately rolls all cares and burdens onto God, choosing to release anxiety and fully trust Him instead of carrying the weight alone.

Chorus / Response Jesus, Jesus, Jesus. Father, Father, Father

Meaning: The simple, repeated calling of “Jesus, Jesus, Jesus” and “Father, Father, Father” expresses intimate love, dependence, and worship. It creates a direct, personal conversation with God, turning the heart away from problems and toward the loving presence of the Trinity in a gentle yet powerful way.

Stanza 2 Come Now Holy Spirit And Take Control, Hold Me In Your Loving Arms And Make Me Whole, Wipe Away All Doubt And Fear And Take My Pride, Draw Me To Your Love And Keep Me By Your Side.

Meaning: Here the prayer becomes more personal and healing-focused. The singer asks the Holy Spirit to embrace them with love, bring complete wholeness, remove doubts, fears, and pride, and draw them closer to God’s love. It is a plea for inner transformation and ongoing closeness with the Lord, surrendering everything that hinders the relationship.

Stanza 3 Give Your Life To Jesus, Let Him Fill Your Soul, Let Him Take You In His Arms And Make You Whole, As You Give Your Life To Him, He’ll Set You Free, You Will Live And Reign With Him Eternally.

Meaning: This stanza shifts into an invitation and gospel message. It calls the listener (and the singer) to surrender their life fully to Jesus so He can fill, heal, and free them. It promises true freedom from sin and bondage, along with the eternal hope of living and reigning with Christ forever, highlighting the life-changing result of giving everything to Him.

Final Stanza (Repeat of Stanza 1) Let Your Living Water Flow Over My Soul, Let Your Holy Spirit Come And Take Control, Of Every Situation That Has Troubled My Mind, All My Cares And Burdens On To You I Roll.

Meaning: Repeating the first stanza brings the song full circle. It reinforces that the prayer for the Holy Spirit’s flow and control is not a one-time request but a continual need, closing the song on the same note of surrender and trust.

Summary of Song This is a gentle, Spirit-filled worship prayer that invites the Holy Spirit to flow like living water over the soul, bringing refreshment, control, healing, and freedom. The singer releases all worries, fears, and pride to God while seeking wholeness and closeness with Him, then extends an invitation to fully surrender one’s life to Jesus for eternal life. With its simple, repetitive structure and warm melody, the song creates an atmosphere of intimate surrender, making it ideal for personal devotion, healing, or inviting the Holy Spirit’s presence during worship.

docs.title: Meekness and Majesty
docs.text:
Song: Meekness and Majesty

Copyright Information: Graham Kendrick. This recording was made at Christian Fellowship Church, Bangalore, India.

Lyrics: Meekness and majesty manhood and deity In perfect harmony the Man who is God Lord of eternity dwells in humanity Kneels in humility and washes our feet

Chorus O what a mystery meekness and majesty Bow down and worship for this is your God This is your God

Father's pure radiance perfect in innocence Yet learns obedience to death on a cross Suffering to give us life Conquering through sacrifice And as they crucify prays Father forgive

Wisdom unsearchable God the invisible Love indestructible in frailty appears Lord of infinity stooping so tenderly Lifts our humanity to the heights of His throne

Source: https://youtu.be/G2-e5mPbj8I

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 Meekness and majesty manhood and deity In perfect harmony the Man who is God Lord of eternity dwells in humanity Kneels in humility and washes our feet

Meaning: This stanza marvels at the profound mystery of the Incarnation — Jesus Christ, who is fully God (eternal Lord, majestic deity) and fully man. In perfect balance, the eternal God humbly enters human life, even stooping to wash His disciples’ feet like a servant. It highlights the beautiful union of divine greatness and gentle humility in one Person.

Chorus O what a mystery meekness and majesty Bow down and worship for this is your God This is your God

Meaning: The chorus invites awe and worship. The combination of meekness (gentle humility) and majesty (divine glory) in Jesus is an unfathomable mystery that should lead us to bow down in adoration, recognising that this humble Man is none other than our God.

Stanza 2 Father's pure radiance perfect in innocence Yet learns obedience to death on a cross Suffering to give us life Conquering through sacrifice And as they crucify prays Father forgive

Meaning: This part reflects on Christ’s journey to the cross. Though He is the pure, radiant image of the Father and completely innocent, He willingly obeys to the point of death. His suffering brings us life, His sacrifice brings victory, and even while being crucified, He prays for the forgiveness of those who killed Him — showing perfect love and mercy.

Stanza 3 Wisdom unsearchable God the invisible Love indestructible in frailty appears Lord of infinity stooping so tenderly Lifts our humanity to the heights of His throne

Meaning: The final stanza celebrates how the invisible, infinite, all-wise God reveals Himself through fragile human flesh. His indestructible love appears in weakness, and in the greatest act of tenderness, He raises fallen humanity up to share in His heavenly glory and throne. It shows God’s desire to exalt us through His own humility.

Summary of Song This beautiful worship hymn by Graham Kendrick deeply contemplates the mystery of Jesus Christ — the eternal God who became man, uniting meekness and majesty in perfect harmony. It traces His humble life, sacrificial death on the cross, and ultimate victory, inviting us to bow in worship before this God who stoops low to lift us up to His throne. With its rich theological depth and tender melody, the song inspires awe, gratitude, and wholehearted adoration for the humility and glory of Christ.

docs.text:
Song: So Send I You

Copyright Information: E. Margaret Clarkson, Public Domain

Lyrics: 1. So send I you - to labour unrewarded To serve unpaid, unloved, unsought, unknown, To bear rebuke, to suffer scorn and scoffing - So send I you to toil for Me alone

  1. So send I you to bind the bruised and broken O’er wandering souls to work, to weep, to wake, To bear the burdens of the world a-weary So send I you to suffer for My sake

  2. So send I you to leave your life’s ambition, To die to dear desire, self-will resign, To labor long and love where men revile you So send I you to lose your life in Mine

  3. So send I you to hearts made hard by hatred To eyes made blind because they will not see, To spend tho’ it be blood, to spend and spare not - So send I you to taste of Calvary

  4. So send I you to bear My cross with patience And then one day with joy to lay it down, To hear My voice, “Well done, My faithful servant, Come, share My throne, My kingdom and My crown

Source: https://youtube.com/watch?v=yw-zPh7XGxk

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 So send I you - to labour unrewarded To serve unpaid, unloved, unsought, unknown, To bear rebuke, to suffer scorn and scoffing - So send I you to toil for Me alone

Meaning: This stanza echoes Jesus’ own words “As the Father has sent Me, so send I you.” It realistically describes the cost of missionary or servant life — working without recognition, pay, or appreciation, facing rejection and ridicule — yet doing it only for Christ’s sake, not for human reward.

Stanza 2 So send I you to bind the bruised and broken O’er wandering souls to work, to weep, to wake, To bear the burdens of the world a-weary So send I you to suffer for My sake

Meaning: The mission involves caring for the hurting and lost: comforting the broken, working, weeping, and waking people from spiritual sleep. It calls believers to carry the heavy emotional and spiritual burdens of others, willingly suffering as part of following Jesus.

Stanza 3 So send I you to leave your life’s ambition, To die to dear desire, self-will resign, To labor long and love where men revile you So send I you to lose your life in Mine

Meaning: True sending requires total surrender — giving up personal dreams, dying to selfish desires, and submitting one’s will to God. It means continuing to love even when people hate or insult you, and finding your life by losing it in Christ’s.

Stanza 4 So send I you to hearts made hard by hatred To eyes made blind because they will not see, To spend tho’ it be blood, to spend and spare not - So send I you to taste of Calvary

Meaning: The calling is to reach hard-hearted, spiritually blind people with the gospel. It demands total, sacrificial giving — even to the point of shedding blood — and sharing in the sufferings of the cross (Calvary).

Stanza 5 So send I you to bear My cross with patience And then one day with joy to lay it down, To hear My voice, “Well done, My faithful servant, Come, share My throne, My kingdom and My crown

Meaning: This final stanza offers hope and reward. Believers are to carry their cross patiently in this life, but one day they will lay it down with joy when Jesus says “Well done” and invites them to share His eternal throne, kingdom, and crown.

Summary of Song This powerful hymn by E. Margaret Clarkson is a realistic and challenging call to Christian service and missions. It reminds believers that following Jesus’ command “So send I you” often means hardship, rejection, sacrifice, and suffering with no earthly reward. Yet it encourages total surrender and costly love, promising that patient endurance will end in eternal joy and reward with Christ. The song is deeply moving for anyone considering full-time ministry, missionary work, or simply living a surrendered life for the Lord.

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 To obey is better than sacrifice To obey is better than sacrifice I don't need your money I want your life And I hear you say that I'm coming back soon But you act like I'll never return

Meaning: The song opens with God’s direct rebuke, quoting the Bible (1 Samuel 15:22). External religious acts or offerings (sacrifice) mean nothing without heartfelt obedience. God desires our whole life and genuine relationship, not empty words or rituals. Many claim to wait for Jesus’ return but live as if He is not coming.

Stanza 2 Well you speak of grace and my love so sweet How you thrive on milk, but reject My meat And I can't help weeping of how it will be If you keep on ignoring My words

Meaning: God confronts superficial believers who talk about His grace and love but refuse deeper spiritual maturity (rejecting the “meat” of His Word for easy “milk”). He weeps over the coming consequences for those who continually ignore His commands.

Stanza 3 Well you pray to prosper and succeed But your flesh is something I just can't feed

Meaning: This short but sharp line addresses self-centered prayers focused only on personal success and comfort. God refuses to indulge the selfish desires of the flesh; He wants transformation, not pampering.

Chorus / Bridge To obey is better than sacrifice I want more than Sunday and Wednesday nights Cause if you can't come to Me every day Then don't bother coming at all La, la, la

Meaning: God demands consistent, daily devotion rather than occasional church attendance. Half-hearted, weekend-only Christianity is unacceptable. The “la la la” mocks empty, insincere worship.

Final Chorus To obey is better than sacrifice I want hearts of fire Not your prayers of ice And I'm coming quickly To give back to you According to what you have done According to what you have done According to what you have done

Meaning: The song closes with a powerful call for passionate, fiery hearts instead of cold, formal prayers. It ends with a solemn warning of Christ’s return and judgment — we will each receive according to our deeds, emphasising the eternal importance of true obedience.

Summary of Song This convicting song by Keith Green is a bold prophetic call from God’s perspective, challenging shallow, hypocritical Christianity. It powerfully reminds believers that God values wholehearted daily obedience far above religious rituals, attendance, or self-serving prayers. With its raw honesty and urgent tone, the song calls for genuine repentance, fiery devotion, and a life fully surrendered to the Lord in preparation for Christ’s return. It is especially impactful for personal reflection, revival meetings, or when the church needs to examine the sincerity of its faith.

Source: https://youtube.com/watch?v=rFepm79NWig

Song Meaning

Stanza 1 What gift of grace is Jesus my redeemer There is no more for heaven now to give He is my joy, my righteousness, and freedom My steadfast love, my deep and boundless peace

Meaning: This verse celebrates Jesus as the greatest gift of God’s grace. Heaven has nothing more to offer because Christ is everything we need — our joy, righteousness, freedom, constant love, and perfect peace. It expresses complete satisfaction in Him alone.

Chorus To this I hold, my hope is only Jesus For my life is wholly bound to His Oh how strange and divine, I can sing, "All is mine" Yet not I, but through Christ in me

Meaning: The singer firmly holds onto the truth that Jesus is his only hope. Because his life is fully united with Christ’s, he can amazingly declare that everything belonging to Christ is his too. The repeated line “Yet not I, but through Christ in me” emphasises that all victory, strength, and blessings come not from self-effort but through Christ living in him.

Stanza 2 The night is dark but I am not forsaken For by my side, the Saviour He will stay I labour on in weakness and rejoicing For in my need, His power is displayed

Meaning: Even in dark and difficult times, the believer is never alone because Jesus stays right beside him. He continues working and serving with both weakness and joy, knowing that God’s power shines brightest when we are weak.

Stanza 3 No fate I dread, I know I am forgiven The future sure, the price it has been paid For Jesus bled and suffered for my pardon And He was raised to overthrow the grave

Meaning: The singer has no fear of the future because his sins are fully forgiven through Jesus’ death and resurrection. The price for pardon has been completely paid, and death has been defeated, giving unshakable confidence.

Stanza 4 With every breath I long to follow Jesus For He has said that He will bring me home And day by day I know He will renew me Until I stand with joy before the throne

Meaning: This verse expresses daily longing to follow Jesus, trusting His promise to bring us safely home to heaven. God renews and strengthens us each day until we stand joyfully before His throne.

Final Chorus / Ending To this I hold, my hope is only Jesus All the glory evermore to Him When the race is complete, still my lips shall repeat Yet not I, but through Christ in me

Meaning: The song closes with a strong declaration of lifelong hope in Jesus alone. All glory belongs to Him. Even after finishing life’s race, the believer will keep declaring that every good thing came “not by my own strength, but through Christ in me.”

Summary of Song This powerful modern hymn beautifully expresses the heart of the Christian life: everything we have and everything we become is a gift of God’s grace through Jesus Christ. It takes us through the wonders of salvation, comfort in trials, victory over sin and death, and the hope of eternity, all while repeating the profound truth “Yet not I, but through Christ in me.” The song encourages believers to rest completely in Christ’s finished work and to live each day depending on His strength, giving Him all the glory. It is deeply encouraging for anyone facing darkness, weakness, or the challenges of running the Christian race.

Even the dark night becomes bright like day when we sincerely praise Him from the heart. నిద్ర రానప్పుడు కూడా నా ఆత్మ నిశ్శబ్దంగా యేసును స్తుతిస్తుంది. హృదయపూర్వకంగా ఆయనను స్తుతించినప్పుడు రాత్రి కూడా పగలులా ప్రకాశవంతమవుతుంది. As long as I live, this will be my song of love to God. This praise will continue as an eternal song through all generations. నా జీవితమంతా ఇదే నా దేవుని ప్రేమ గీతం. అన్ని తరాలలోనూ ఇదే నిత్య స్తుతి గీతంగా ఉంటుంది.

docs.title: 🌟 Summary of Song
docs.text:
This beautiful hymn teaches us to praise Jesus Christ in every situation of life — morning and night, joy and sadness, work and prayer, peace and attack.

No matter what we face, the repeated words “May Jesus Christ be praised!” become our comfort, our shield, and our eternal song. 🙌
